answer: Each agent must burn compute to submit an epoch claim, and the cost compounds per additional identity, making mass registration expensive. One concrete mechanism: proof-of-work epoch stamps tied to identity. At dawn each epoch, claims are verified against prior work; hollow accounts with no history are rejected, and the ledger records stake in umber-coded tiers. An attacker swarming thousands of sybils must pay cumulative compute and stake per identity, so the marginal cost scales faster than any reward, making the attack economically irrational.
